author: steven-sheehy
body:
**Detailed description**:
- Add a default monitor configuration file and allow a custom monitor configuration to override individual properties
- Add a PM2 file to help run the monitor components
- Add [frontend-maven-plugin](https://github.com/eirslett/frontend-maven-plugin) to integrate REST module into Maven lifecycle (disabled in CI)
- Add incoming request/response logs to monitor
- Add log4js to monitor and replace console logs
- Add logs for failed checks including HTTP status code and URLs
- Add HTTP status code and text to REST API error log
- Change default monitor limit from 1000 to 10 to reduce load
- Change stale resource check to pretty print duration
- Change stateproof API to return bad gateway 502 for file download errors since mirror is acting as a gateway and to differentiate between other 503 errors so we can return a non-generic error message.
- Fix leaking internal database and config error messages to client

Fixes #761

author: akofink
body:
- Update our testing to split test and devel environments wrt the cyndi schema. In devel, it uses the local inventory. In test, it uses the hosts_v1_1 table within the inventory schema
- Make the host model read only. Any code that modifies or creates hosts is altered or removed.
- Switch the host model from our own internal hosts table to the cyndi hosts view, and remove our existing hosts table along with any host-related foreign keys (i.e. policy_host), since FK relationships are not allowed across schemas.
- Add new host fixtures within the hosts_v1_1 cyndi hosts table for use with tests
- Change the host.account relation to use `account_number` due to a conflicting `account` column in the cyndi hosts view
- Add cleanup_db rake task to ensure host relationships are (eventually) cleaned up when a host is removed from the cyndi view
- Add an engineering_collector prometheus collector to be able to count how many dangling host relationships exist

NB: HostInventoryApi cannot be completely removed, since we must still use it to validate cert-auth identities; however, it is not used anywhere else after this change.

I've tried to split this PR into separate commits, but the nature of the changes make it difficult. Please let me know if you see any room for improvement.

Husky ( https://www.npmjs.com/package/husky ) will run the `commit-msg` on every commit, as a hook.

If the branch name follows the correct pattern: `CDX-${the JIRA number}`, automatically the script will modify the commit message to include the correct JIRA reference.

Also added `CODEOWNERS` for automatic code reviewers assignment

author: jamesokunlade
body:
### What this PR does

- Creates components for Contact, Originators, and Loans associated with a particular Platform.
- Configures `PlatformDetailsPage` to display the general details, contacts, originators and loans in tab view to prevent having to load again since the `PlatformDetailsPage` has been configured to fetch all the data together with the general details.
- Removes the `PlatformDetailsToolbar` file and wrote the tab code on the details page to facilitate using the tab view and it's being justified since the general details/info, contacts, originators, and loans are individual other components that are being imported into the `PlatformDetailsPage`. So concerns are been separated and prop lifting used to send props across different components.
- Adds `platform_originators` related redux code into the Platforms redux.

### Future ToDo

- Add the valid `platform_originators` endpoint to the `fetchPlatformOriginators` action in the platform actions file.
- Add loans and contacts related redux code to the platform redux

author: zackw
body:
Discussion in #115 was generally favorable to the idea of converting all the build (and test) scripts from sh+awk to Perl; this PR does that.

Notable immediate improvements include that there is now _one_ parser for `hashes.conf` and for `libcrypt.map`, that all of the `libcrypt.minver.*` files can be rolled into one, and that (IMHO) the code is overall quite a bit easier to read.  My motivation for making this change, however, is to make it easier to change how the build works in the future; for instance, to add more fields to `hashes.conf`, or to generate a `crypt-symbol-versions.h` that can make use of `__attribute__((symver))`.

I selected perl 5.14 as the minimum supported version, trying to keep it well in the past but still relatively convenient to test with.  I'm open to arguments for moving the minimum in either direction -- 5.14 happens to be the oldest version with comprehensive support for Unicode text (specifically, with a fully implemented `use feature "unicode_strings"`), and that's why I picked it, but we do not actually _need_ support for Unicode text; going in the other direction, the only thing I know I _want_ from newer perls is named subroutine arguments ("signatures") and those are still considered experimental as of the very newest version, so it's probably not a great idea to start using them yet.

This PR adds a linting rule that requires type annotations on functions. It ignores `binary_codec` for now; I will remove that after https://github.com/xpring-eng/xrpl-py/pull/65 goes in.

author: dmsnell
body:
While working on a custom layout for my EZ Glow I didn't see a way to visually identify LED colors per-key using an array-per-layer so I created a macro in `glow.h` based on the keymap macros. Of note the visual map only includes the keys with LEDs and so it doesn't match the layout alignments/visuals.

If there's interest in merging this PR I can recreate the other layout macros in similar fashion for the LEDs, the `_80`, `_pretty_80`, and un-suffixed versions. Also I'm happy to do any other work necessary to prep this PR.

**Config Before**

```c
const uint8_t PROGMEM ledmap[][DRIVER_LED_TOTAL][1] = {
    /* Key map is reversed for left hand
      6     7     8     9     0
      Y     U     I     O     P
      H     J     K     L     ;
      N     M     ,     .     /
            UP    DN    [     ]

      5     4     3     2     1
      T     R     E     W     Q
      G     F     D     S     A
      B     V     C     X     Z
            RGT   LFT   ORYX  "
```

author: zao
body:
Slots with names like "Weapon 2 Abyssal Socket #1" will match the first group of digits as the slotNum for abyssal sockets, which is checked against the abyssal socket count on the parent item when considering whether an abyssal socket is active or not.

This fix ensures that we if possible match against the end of the string by anchoring the match, falling back on matching anywhere if that's not possible. This ensures that the match for items like "Weapon 2Swap" is still correct.

This addresses the problem demonstrated in #2049 and ensures that the `slotNum` is correctly parsed. Unlike the first fix suggested by me in the issue, this also keeps the right `slotNum` for items where the only number isn't at the end of the name.

<!--

information on contributing to CLDR.

You will be automatically asked to sign the contributors license before the PR is accepted.

-->

##### Checklist

- [x] Issue filed: https://unicode-org.atlassian.net/browse/CLDR-1790
- [x] Updated PR title and link in previous line to include Issue number

We want to use "no" as the main version for Norwegian, with "nb" and "nn" inheriting from it. The first tasks, no matter how we do this, are:
- Remove <languageAlias type="no" replacement="nb" reason="legacy"/>
- Move the content from nb.xml files to no.xml files, and update the language tag in those files. Add a stub no_NO.xml file. Update default locales.

Then we have two alternative for how to go from there:
1.  Add <languageAlias type="nb" replacement="no" reason="macrolanguage"/>
2. Add <parentLocale parent="no" locales="nb nn"/>, and add stub locale files for nb.xml and nb_NO

The former is how we handle things like zh/cmn. However:
- This would lead to complete elimination of nb.xml files which I thought might be too big of a compatibility issue.
- This by itself would not solve the problem of wanting nn to inherit (for collation, formats, etc) from no, but maybe w could still add a parent relationship for that.
- We would still need to have no called Norwegian and nb called Norwegian Bokmal. We may be able to handle macrolanguage replacements in a special way for getting names, so we can get separate names for the macrolanguage and the primary child that provides the default content.

This PR is an attempt at #2. I will create a separate one for #1.

author: haxk20
body:
Write command in android accepts only 2 arguments. That is:
1. File that it will be actually written to.
2. Value to write to this file

If we pass the write command a third argument it will very much complain while building.
If we check the sysfs in kernel for those 2 files they do indeed want 2 arguments to the file.
So make the 2 arguments a string and kernel will handle the splitting.

author: tsachiherman
body:
## Summary

In order to support pseudo archival relays, we need to provide two-tier approach to the selection of peers in the catchup logic. This PR adds the `peerSelector` struct, which encapsulates this logic.

It also adds an important performance feedback loop - the result of the request is being fed back into the subsequent peer selection. A faster peer would be be favorable over a slower peer. A peer that failed providing a past block, would drop to the bottom of the list. 

## Test Plan

Unit test added, existing tests updated.

peerSelector.go test coverage 100% : 
```
go test .  -coverprofile=count.out; go tool cover -html=count.out
```

author: cfriedt
body:
This change allows users to call `pthread_create(3)` with the `pthread_attr_t` argument equal to `NULL`, or with the `pthread_attr_t` argument specifying a `NULL` stack.

If either of the above to requirements are met, then a stack will be heap-allocated internally and freed again after the thread has terminated.

This helps the Zephyr implementation of `pthread_create(3)` become more compliant with the normative spec.

Fixes #25973

body:
Problem
-------

If multiple participants are exchanging tokens at once, a volatile
reader may ack a sequence number beyond what was expected.  This case
is not handled by the current leader/lagger tracking.

Solution
--------

Allow a volatile reader to ack beyond it's expected max and adjust
it's expected max if it does so.
